asks: recurrenceRule is typed as a bare string with no grammar. The app invented one to run at all — ratify it, or specify a different one?
because: RecurringTask declares "recurrenceRule" as valueType "string" and the spec text says nothing about its form, so the implementation had to choose: it accepts "daily | weekly | monthly" and "every N day(s)|week(s)|month(s)", and reports anything else as unschedulable. That grammar is already load-bearing in app/src/domain/recurrence.ts, so this is not a suggestion — it is a decision that has already been made under duress and needs either blessing or replacing.

options.label: Ratify the invented grammar
options.detail: Promotes the rule format to a named attribute-type so the grammar lives in the glossary rather than in one implementation file. Readable, matches what already runs, and covers only fixed intervals — no "first Monday of the month", no end dates.

proposal.summary: Give recurrenceRule a named type with a stated grammar

ops.spec: A repeating interval, written as "daily", "weekly", "monthly", or "every N days" / "every N weeks" / "every N months" where N is a positive whole number. Case-insensitive. A month step lands on the same day of the following month, clamped to that month's last day. Anything outside this grammar is rejected rather than guessed at.

tests: "monthly" advances 2026-01-31 to 2026-02-28, clamped to the shorter month
"every other Tuesday" is rejected rather than interpreted

options.label: Use RFC 5545 RRULE
options.detail: The calendar standard — complete, interoperable with anything that speaks iCalendar, and covers cases the invented grammar cannot express. The cost is that an end-user writing specs cannot read or write "FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2" without help, which cuts against the point of a human-readable shared vocabulary. It also means rewriting the app's recurrence code rather than blessing it.

proposal.summary: Type recurrenceRule as an RFC 5545 recurrence rule

ops.spec: A recurrence rule in RFC 5545 (iCalendar) RRULE form, such as "FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2" or "FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=1MO". The full RRULE grammar applies, including BYDAY, COUNT and UNTIL. Rules that do not parse as RRULE are rejected.

tests: "every 2 weeks" is rejected — it is not RRULE
